newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, with gains expected from light hog marketings as intense heat and humidity return to the corn belt, livestock dealers said.
Temperatures well above 90 degrees Fahrenheit were forecast for the western belt on Friday and seen extending eastward Saturday and Sunday, meteorologists said.

However, a cold front was expected to move in later Monday, bringing temperatures back to normal. But the hot weather Friday through Sunday was expected to keep movement light early Monday, the dealers said.
"I don't see many hogs moving, unless something happens over the weekend we don't know about," one central Illinois hog buyer said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen $58.50 to $59.00.
Illinois hog prices at the plant were expected to range $58.50 to $59.00 and Indiana/Ohio top prices were seen at $59.00 to $59.50, the dealers said.
Cash hog prices on Monday also could be underpinned if this week's steep declines in pork prices spurs renewed retail buying, market sources said.
The number two carcass cut-out value on Thursday closed at $76.50 per cwt, down $0.54 from Wednesday and down $4.93 since prices turned lower on Monday, USDA statistics showed.
